subproblem.title: Subsequential closedness in B_1(0) gives eventual ε-neighbourhood inclusion (compactness step of parent (A.3)(3))
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, S ⊆ ℝ^P and S_k ⊆ ℝ^P (k ∈ ℕ). Assume that whenever sub : ℕ → ℕ is strictly increasing, z_k ∈ B_1(0) ∩ S_{sub(k)} for every k, and z_k → x in ℝ^P, then x ∈ S. Then for every ε > 0 there is k₀ ∈ ℕ such that B_1(0) ∩ S_k ⊆ {x : there is z ∈ S with |x − z| < ε} for every k ≥ k₀ (open unit ball B_1(0), Euclidean distance).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (S : Set (Euclid P)) (Ss : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)), (∀ (sub : ℕ → ℕ) (z : ℕ → Euclid P) (x : Euclid P), StrictMono sub → (∀ k, z k ∈ ball (0 : Euclid P) 1 ∩ Ss (sub k)) → Tendsto z atTop (𝓝 x) → x ∈ S) → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ k₀ : ℕ, ∀ k ≥ k₀, ball (0 : Euclid P) 1 ∩ Ss k ⊆ {x | ∃ z ∈ S, dist x z < ε}
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Appendix A, hypothesis A.3(3) (book/chapter-A.txt lines 31–32: "If φ, φ_k ∈ F with φ_k ⇀ φ, then for each ε > 0 there is a k(ε) such that B_1(0) ∩ sing φ_k ⊆ {x : dist(sing φ, x) < ε} for all k ≥ k(ε)"), which Simon asserts follows from (12) in the proof of 7.3.3 (chapter-07.txt lines 478–491: "It now follows from (10), (11), (12) and 2.4 that all the hypotheses of Theorem A.4 … are satisfied") without writing out the compactness step. This lemma is that step, as carried out in the parent proof, step 7 (A.3)(3), the contradiction-and-compactness argument: "Suppose the conclusion fails. Then there are k_1 < k_2 < … and w_j ∈ B_1(0) ∩ sing φ_{μ_{k_j}} with dist(w_j, z) ≥ ε for all z ∈ sing φ_μ. … After passing to a further subsequence, w_j → w with |w| ≤ 1 … Then dist(w_j, w) ≥ ε for all j, contradicting w_j → w." It is stated here for arbitrary sets S_k, S; in the parent, S_k = sing φ_k and S = sing φ_μ, and the hypothesis is supplied there by step 6 and the sibling threshold_limit.
Notation. N_ε(S) := {x : there is z ∈ S with |x − z| < ε}.
1. Fix ε > 0 and suppose, for contradiction, that no k₀ works: for every k₀ there is k ≥ k₀ with B_1(0) ∩ S_k ⊄ N_ε(S). For such k pick x ∈ B_1(0) ∩ S_k with x ∉ N_ε(S); then |x − z| ≥ ε for every z ∈ S (otherwise x ∈ N_ε(S)). Hence the property Bad(k): "there is x ∈ B_1(0) ∩ S_k with |x − z| ≥ ε for every z ∈ S" holds for arbitrarily large k, i.e. frequently along atTop.
2. By Filter.extraction_of_frequently_atTop there is a strictly increasing sub : ℕ → ℕ with Bad(sub(j)) for every j. By choice, pick z_j ∈ B_1(0) ∩ S_{sub(j)} with |z_j − z| ≥ ε for every z ∈ S.
3. Every z_j lies in the closed ball B̄_1(0), which is compact because ℝ^P is a proper space (isCompact_closedBall). By sequential compactness (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq) there are x ∈ B̄_1(0) and a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ with z_{ψ(i)} → x as i → ∞.
4. The map sub ∘ ψ is strictly increasing (StrictMono.comp), z_{ψ(i)} ∈ B_1(0) ∩ S_{sub(ψ(i))} for every i, and z_{ψ(i)} → x. By the hypothesis (applied to the indices sub ∘ ψ and the points i ↦ z_{ψ(i)}), x ∈ S.
5. Since z_{ψ(i)} → x, there is i with |z_{ψ(i)} − x| < ε (Metric.tendsto_atTop). But x ∈ S, so step 2 gives |z_{ψ(i)} − x| ≥ ε. This contradiction shows that some k₀ satisfies B_1(0) ∩ S_k ⊆ N_ε(S) for all k ≥ k₀. ∎
proof_key_steps: If the conclusion fails for some ε, then for infinitely many k there is a point of B_1(0) ∩ S_k at distance ≥ ε from every point of S.
Extract a strictly increasing sub with such points z_j ∈ B_1(0) ∩ S_{sub(j)} (extraction_of_frequently_atTop and choice).
By compactness of B̄_1(0), a further subsequence z_{ψ(i)} converges to some x; the hypothesis (indices sub ∘ ψ) gives x ∈ S.
Then |z_{ψ(i)} − x| < ε for some i, contradicting the choice of the z_j.

audit.reason: Failure yields strictly increasing bad indices. Compactness of the closed unit ball supplies a convergent further subsequence; the hypothesis places its limit in S, contradicting uniform separation. No closedness assumption on S is missing.
